text: A Campaign Legal Center complaint cited 100+ undisclosed stock trades (2024); Florida Bulldog reported inaccurate financial disclosures and charter-school contracts tied to his wife's firms. Collier School Board member Kelly Mason filed a second assault lawsuit in July 2026, which he calls political. WLRN found a Donalds ad deceptively edited a Jolly clip on gender-affirming care.
source: Florida Bulldog, WLRN, Campaign Legal Center

text: Jolly declined every general-election debate with Donalds, citing the Republican's 'repeated lies'; Donalds' ads brand it a 'debate dodge' and call his shifts on abortion and guns after leaving the GOP fraudulent. His 2016 Senate campaign admitted editing his Wikipedia page to remove Scientology and lobbying references.

As Attorney General, Moody's office approved the 2024 Centene Medicaid settlement that steered $10M to the Hope Florida Foundation; the money then flowed to political committees fighting the 2024 marijuana amendment. Experts told PolitiFact she is responsible for her office's actions, though no charges were filed and a grand jury's findings were expunged. She has also skipped debates and town halls.

Nixon drew bipartisan backlash after declining in a CBS interview to call Cuba's government a dictatorship, a statement she later walked back (Oct 27). A conservative watchdog's complaint alleges about $270K in missing charitable funds tied to her Cafe Resistance nonprofit; it is an allegation, not a finding. The Florida House reprimanded her in May 2026 for using a megaphone during the redistricting debate, where she was also arrested at a sit-in.
source: Axios Miami, NBC6 (Oct 27, 2026), Washington Free Beacon

text: A Wall Street Journal report, summarized by the Tampa Bay Times, said Luna may have passed inside information to influencer Rogan O'Handley for Polymarket bets. The Times later reported DOJ never received a referral, and Luna's lawyers sent the paper a cease-and-desist. Leela Gray's ads cite the story; Luna's campaign sent Gray a cease-and-desist in return.
source: Tampa Bay Times (July 20 & Aug 3, 2026), Floridian Press

text: A federal judge held Uthmeier in civil contempt in June 2025 for telling police they could keep enforcing a blocked immigration law. A leaked Leon County grand jury report said $10M from a Medicaid settlement was 'misappropriated' via Hope Florida while he was the Governor's chief of staff; it found insufficient evidence to charge him and an appeals court ordered the findings struck. Rodríguez's ads call him 'the root of corruption.'

Florida Bulldog reported that Ingoglia's Form 6 financial disclosure omits 100+ properties worth about $10M held through four LLCs; his office says the form is accurate. County leaders in Broward, Orange and Seminole disputed his 'DOGE' wasteful-spending figures, and his office sent armed agents to a Vietnam veteran who mailed him a critical postcard.

Reporters traced St. Pete Shines money through chains of PACs to Duke Energy, TECO and FPL-parent interests, including a PAC registered at a UF fraternity house, while the city studies its Duke franchise; Ark Invest gave big days after its Trop-site bid was snubbed. Crist skipped the July 28 Tiger Bay forum (the empty chair became a prop) and agreed to only one runoff debate, on Bay News 9 Oct 13.
source: Tampa Bay Times, Axios, Florida Trib (Aug 2026), Creative Loafing

text: The Rays backed out of the Gas Plant stadium deal in spring 2025, and Welch rejected a Moffitt Cancer Center campus deal whose developer sought a roughly $19M land discount. Tampa Bay Times editor Graham Brink cited the deputy mayor's resignation amid hostile-workplace claims, low City Hall attendance, transparency problems and campaign-finance lapses. Florida Politics, whose publisher's wife chairs the pro-Crist committee, published an affair allegation Welch called 'a disgusting and flat-out lie.'
source: Tampa Bay Times, Florida Politics, Creative Loafing

text: In 2022 the Tampa Bay Times published 2020 screenshots in which Peters appeared to take the 'QAnon oath,' called the 2020 election 'Trump 2Q2Q,' and shared a post calling the moon landing, 9/11 and the pandemic hoaxes; asked if she believed them she said 'I have no idea,' then said she does not follow QAnon. On the board she helped lead efforts to remove library books. The Times' Oct 2026 recommendation revisits the episode and says she has since softened some stances.
source: Tampa Bay Times (Oct 2022; Oct 1, 2026), TBN Weekly

tag: AI Super PAC Ads & New College
text: Kirschner's campaign accused Gruters of benefiting from roughly $2.5M in AI-generated super PAC ads it called false. Her tenure at the New College Foundation drew a former board member's demand for an audit of restricted donor funds and a 2025 scholarship lawsuit; she called the claims baseless. Primary rivals said she owed Trump's endorsement to her husband's connections.
source: Tampa Bay Times (Oct 21, 2026), WUSF, Herald-Tribune, Bradenton Times

who: David Glenn Jr. vs. Kathleen Peters (County Commission Dist 6)
text: Pinellas sheriff's deputies checked on Democratic challenger David Glenn Jr. after he posted '#86Peters' hashtags and an Oct 4 photo of seashells spelling '86 Peters,' which some read as a threat and Glenn described as campaign slang for defeating her. Incumbent Kathleen Peters said she did not file the report.
